demand.reason: Global primary tungsten consumption is estimated at approximately 81,000 metric tons annually, placing it securely within the moderate-demand band of 10,000–100,000 tons.

growth.reason: Demand projects low growth (1-5% CAGR), driven by stable volume expansions in cemented carbides for industrial machine cutting, mining drills, and heavy infrastructure, supplemented by rearmament spikes in military kinetic ammunition.

supplier_concentration.reason:
Mining: Extraction is highly concentrated. China produced 67,000 of the 85,000 tons mined in 2025 (79%), placing primary mining diversity in the 65–85% band (Score 4).


Refining: Downstream processing of ore into ammonium paratungstate (APT) and carbide powder is overwhelmingly dominated by China, which controls an estimated 83% of the refining market share, in the 65–85% band (Score 4).

reserves.reason:
Time-frame: World reserves are more than 4.7 million tons, about 55 years of supply at 2025 mine output of 85,000 tons, in the 50–100 year band (Score 2).


Diversification: China holds 53% of world reserves alongside Australia (12%) and Russia (9%). The calculated HHI is about 0.31, placing the geographic endowment in the moderately concentrated band.

end_use.reason:
Defense & National Security (+1.5): essential for armor-piercing kinetic energy penetrators, anti-tank munitions, and heavy missile alloys. Electrification & Transport (+1.0): required for high-performance aerospace structural alloys and machine tool manufacturing. Construction & Heavy Industry (+0.5): cemented tungsten carbides form the structural backbone for global mining and construction machinery. Healthcare & Biomedical (+1.0): utilized widely for medical radiation shielding in X-ray systems and precise dental tools.


Sector presence scores total 4.0 across 4 qualifying sectors. The breadth bonus adds +1.5, yielding an objective composite score of 5.5.

substitutability_recyclability.reason:
Substitutability: Molybdenum carbide, titanium carbide, and cermets substitute in cutting tools with moderate hardness and wear performance penalties. Depleted uranium acts as a commercial military alternative in kinetic penetrators, matching Score 2.


Recyclability: Secondary recovery is well-established. Carbide tool scrap is routinely collected, and recycling loops supply approximately 30–40% of apparent consumption, tracking within the 20–40% moderate recycling tier.

extraction_refining.reason: Tungsten mining uses standard flotation, but refining requires complex chemical processing to yield high-purity ammonium paratungstate (APT) via caustic pressure leaching and crystallization, classifying it as complex and specialized.

upcoming_projects.reason: The project pipeline is adequate. Imminent restarts of massive brownfield assets like the Sangdong mine in South Korea, alongside active new developments in Australia (Dolphin), are securely capable of adding 10–20% to supply within 3–5 years.

india_position.reason:
Import Dependence: India possesses small, uneconomic occurrences in Rajasthan and is >80% reliant on imported concentrates and refined powders to satisfy its advanced defense and manufacturing tools, pacing at the marginal domestic production band.


Strategic Posture: Tungsten is notified on India's critical minerals list with customs duties exempted. Hindustan Zinc won a tungsten block in Andhra Pradesh in November 2025, putting a concrete domestic plan in motion, though there is no KABIL mandate or foreign equity investment (Score 2).

price_volatility.reason: Tungsten prices exhibited extreme volatility after China's February 2025 export controls and reduced mining quotas. Chinese scheelite concentrate rose from 142,750 yuan/t at the end of 2024 to 680,500 yuan/t in February 2026, about 4.8 times, and domestic APT passed 1 million yuan/t (SMM). USGS's annual average concentrate price rose from $252 (2024) to about $380 per metric ton unit (2025). This meets the extreme band (Score 5).

capability.name: Tungsten
capability.next_move: Chemical (APT) recycling so scrap is processed at home; mine later.
capability.what_india_has: Sandvik's carbide-recycling plant at Chiplun; HZL's tungsten block; a large tooling industry that generates scrap.

stages.world: China 79%; then Vietnam and Kazakhstan. Korea's Sangdong began processing in 2026.
stages.india: HZL won a block in Andhra Pradesh (Nov 2025); Degana tendered.

stages.world: APT conversion: China dominant; Austria, Vietnam and Germany outside.

stages.india: Sandvik's Chiplun plant recycles carbide into powder.

stages.world: Cutting tools, mining bits, defence, electronics.
stages.india: Tool and defence demand; India exports tungsten scrap.

strategyList.name: Tungsten chemistry (APT) and carbide recycling
strategyList.what: Leaching concentrate or scrap, purifying, crystallising ammonium paratungstate (APT), then reducing and carburising to powder.
strategyList.outside_china: China dominant; Austria, Vietnam, Germany; Korea's Sangdong mine (concentrate from 2026).
strategyList.india_base: Sandvik's Chiplun carbide recycling; HZL tungsten block; tooling scrap.

strategyList.name: Recycling (batteries, magnets, catalysts, PV)
strategyList.what: Shredding and hydrometallurgy of black mass; magnet recovery; spent-catalyst leaching; PV-panel recovery.
strategyList.outside_china: Battery recycling: China has over three-quarters of pre-treatment and 90% of material-recovery capacity; Europe, Japan, Korea and the US smaller.
strategyList.cost: India's scheme expects ~Rs 8,000 crore for 270+ kt/yr of capacity (~Rs 30 crore per kt/yr), yielding ~40 kt/yr of critical minerals.
strategyList.india_base: Lohum, Rubamin, the Bhopal magnet facility, CSIR-NML; Rs 1,500 crore incentive scheme (2025).
